items.title: The Killings: Parrish Station
items.reason: A complete six-episode dual-timeline murder mystery whose structure strongly matches the profile: Georgia Cooke investigates the 1987 massacre and, decades later, copycat killings reopen the case. The episode progression supplies meaningful information throughout rather than reserving everything for the finale: the Bone Gospel is established as real, a present-day podcaster body extends the copycat case, an older similar case is uncovered, evidence links the murder mysteries, the ritual and signal become concrete, and the penultimate episode identifies that the killer has been close to the investigators before the finale becomes a race to stop Callum Parrish. The Guardian independently characterizes the series as a murder mystery packed with twists and outlandish momentum. The main weakness is that the occult/cosmic-horror explanation makes the clue chain less grounded than a conventional procedural, and interpersonal estrangement/obsession adds a substantial drama layer, but the complete-season evidence supports frequent progressive answers, active investigation, mystery, culprit pursuit and sustained suspense.
